instruction: Use the set square to push the three blocks into a straight, aligned row.

frames.label: turn 1: ONE ROW ALONG THE SET SQUARE'S EDGE: the set square is the long bar lying in front of the three cubes, and its long straight edge is the ruler everything is lined up to - the bar is what the hand moves, the cubes are what come to it. A cube is never picked up and never touched by the fingers: it is driven ahead of that edge until a whole face of it lies flat on the edge, and three faces on that one edge is the row. A cube is finished when there is no strip of bare table left between it and the edge, and no wedge of table at the corner where it meets the edge; while either of those is still visible that cube is not in the row yet and the bar has to go forward again, square to its own long edge. Nothing has been pushed yet - take hold of the bar at its middle, level with the three cubes, so that one pass sweeps all of them, and keep it down on the table: this grasp is for pushing, not for lifting. Right now the left cube is still short of the bar, with a strip of bare table between them; the middle cube is still short of the bar, with a strip of bare table between them; the right cube is still short of the bar, with a strip of bare table between them. orient the gripper and travel over the set square

A cube is finished when there is no strip of bare table left between it and the edge, and no wedge of table at the corner where it meets the edge; while either of those is still visible that cube is not in the row yet and the bar has to go forward again, square to its own long edge. All three cubes now have a whole face on the edge and lie in one row, so the pushing is over. The bar is not part of the row: lift it straight up off the table and carry it away through the air - never slide it back along the table, because it is pressed against the cubes and dragging it turns them out of line again - then set it down clear of them and put both arms back where they started. Do not let go and take another pushing pass: the row is already made, and pushing it a second time only knocks it out of line. return both arms to their initial pose
